traditional_solar.title: Surya Siddhanta

sources.reference: Table of Revolutions and Present Position of the Apsides and Nodes of the Planets; Sun row, A.D. 1850
verified_claims: The table lists 387 solar-apsis revolutions per aeon.
The table heading specifies years per arcminute of motion; the Sun's listed rate is approximately 516.8 years per arcminute.
The resulting traditional solar-apsis position for A.D. 1850 is 95 degrees 4 minutes.
The table separately lists a true position of 100 degrees 22 minutes for A.D. 1850.
The published mean solar longitude for January 1, 1860, midnight at Ujjayini is 257 degrees, 48 minutes, 7 seconds.
The solar revolution count is 4320000 over 1577917828 civil days.
The traditional true-place method applies a correction for the apsis.
The correction requires additional traditional parameters and calculation steps.

notes: The current implementation calculates mean solar longitude from a published reference position.
